absent: Ring sizing, mapping, event harvesting and completion wakeup behavior beyond header layout and lock ownership.
Request allocation, submission, cancellation, reference lifetime and error propagation.
Eventfd signaling rules and wait queue usage for poll and ring waits.
Security hook effects for file allocation and dentry binding and their failure modes.
Slow dentry teardown, shrinker interaction and final free after fast path declines.
Global async quota accounting, limit enforcement and sysctl handler range checks.
Backing address and file operations for the private ring file beyond their declarations.
Cache lifecycle for operation, context and inode slabs and mount setup teardown.

findings.text: Ring magic equals hex a10a10a1 with compatible level 1 and incompatible level 0, and the internal kiocb key equals 0.
Plug batching threshold equals 2, embedded folio cache holds 8 entries, and system wide async ceiling defaults to hex 10000.
Under fs the async controls appear as aio-nr with mode 0444 and aio-max-nr with mode 0644, each sized as unsigned long.

Shared completion ring header records internal index, capacity in events, producer and consumer positions, magic discriminator, feature levels and header size, followed by variable length event storage with documented footprint near 128 bytes plus ring area.
Context table combines deferred free header with count and flexible array, per cpu shard holds locally available slots, and quiescence waiter combines completion with waiter count.

Async context state comprises user and request references, liveness flag, user identifier, per cpu shards, batch quantum, user supplied maximum, event capacity, mapped window, folio vector and page count, deferred free work, quiescence waiter, isolated groups for availability count, cancellation list, ring wait, completion position and counter, embedded folio store, backing file and numeric id.

Sync variant associates file with deferred work, data only selector and credential, while poll variant associates file with queue head, event mask, cancellation and scheduling state, wait linkage and deferred work.

Per operation control overlays file pointer with read write, sync and poll forms, and common tail holds owning context, cancel callback, result event, cancellation linkage, reference count and optional event delivery context used only when user resfd is nonzero.
Async inode wrapper extends base inode with migration lock and back pointer to owning context, recoverable from the base inode.

User supplied maximum only charges global quota while effective capacity derives from event count minus one, and slot availability is tracked by shared atomic moderated through per cpu batching to prevent ring overflow.

Cancellation membership is protected by context lock, ring head and waiting belong to ring mutex, and completion position with completed total belongs to completion lock, each in a separately aligned group; ring head is also writable from user space.

Global async totals have a dedicated lock, async inode migration has its own lock, and file state uses a spinlock for general fields with a position mutex meaningful for atomic position and directory cases.

Private ring file is anchored on the async mount with custom address handling, context linkage and size proportional to page count, exposed under a fixed short pseudo name with read write access and ring file handling, with inode dropped if file creation fails.
Visible setup consists of private ring file creation and filesystem control registration, where registration is present in one build and compiled to no operation in another.
File layer exposes pseudo creation from inode mount name flags and operations, empty allocation from flags and credential, and queries for current and ceiling file counts.

File count enforcement denies unprivileged creation at ceiling after exact recheck, reports ENOMEM for allocation failure and ENFILE for table exhaustion, accounts success in the global tally, and emits ceiling notice only on new peak.

A usable file owns a credential reference subject to security approval, initialized general and position locking, cleared path and readahead, access mode derived from open flags, default suppression of permission and content notification, detached operations mapping private inode owner and poll state, zeroed io flags position and error baselines, with the reference established last for safe reuse.

Attached path determines inode and mapping with sampled error baselines, seek read and write capabilities reflect both access mode and operation support, sync related io hints derive from open flags, and read only opens take an extra read hold.
Access mode derives from open flags by increment and mask, append direct dsync and sync each map to distinct io hints, and notification mode replacement preserves unrelated mode bits.
File reference setup stores one less than the logical count to compensate atomic bias.
Dentry layer exposes pseudo allocation, inode binding, reference release, and predicates for positive, negative, miss, lookup and external name states.

Allocated dentries start with self parentage, no inode, inherited superblock operations and flags, initialized reference sequence and list state, NUL terminated name with long name spill to counted external store and ordered publication, optional initializer with full cleanup on failure, and global dentry accounting.

Pseudo path construction rejects directories and yields non RCU dentries with anonymous naming and held mount before inode binding, while pseudo file construction compensates ownership transfer on failure and suppresses notification by default.

Binding requires a negative entry with security interposition, acquires inode before dentry lock, publishes inode with type under sequence protection, and refreshes parent watched state while holding the dentry lock; the refresh is inert in one build.

Entry typing maps missing to miss, directories with capability caching, links with get capability to symlink, regular files to regular and other modes to special, adding automount demand when the inode bears the automount mark.
Parent watched state tracks whether the parent inode mask expresses interest in child events and overlaps the possible child event set; evaluation uses a single consistent mask read.

Mount acquisition tolerates null and resolves the enclosing mount before counting, name construction pairs text with length, inode count is observed atomically with positive count required for hold, and path release drops dentry before mount.

Dentry release prefers lockless last reference handling under RCU with fallback to locked revalidation, retaining entries that remain referenced or cache eligible and delegating the remainder to slow teardown; retention excludes unhashed, disconnected, delete advised and dontcache forms and otherwise guarantees LRU presence with referenced marking only under lock.
Creation chains unwind ownership in reverse with null tolerant release and compensating holds, covering pseudo file, path, long name spill, dentry cache and anonymous inode resources.

Concurrent readers can observe transient name and flag bytes, a zero count reached without the lock does not prove exclusivity, binding a positive entry or binding during lookup violates preconditions, and position lock storage is shared with other uses for files without atomic position.

Approximate per cpu tallies must be validated before enforcement, LRU insertion requires absence from both LRU and shrink membership, and negative accounting is adjusted only when the entry currently lives solely on the LRU.
